applicability.scope: Assessing distributed checkpoint recovery through DLRover memory agreement, persistence completion and replica transport, and NVIDIA Resiliency Extension complete-iteration selection; distinguishes worker, host and replica loss and separates queued saves, publication, application-state validity and durable recovery. Save performance belongs to dcp-async-save-performance
applicability.prerequisites: The pinned sources and limits are read; reading authorizes no launchers, failure injection or checkpoint loading, and restore evidence needs separate authorization
applicability.input_contract: The declared failure domain; actual memory, storage and replica placement and helper lifetime; step or iteration identity, the expected shard/rank set and finalization result; the application's model, optimizer and caller-required RNG/scheduler/data-position state contract; the target environment's format and world-size/replication assumptions
applicability.produced_artifact: An answer to each of the four acceptance questions (snapshot survival, cross-participant completeness, application-state completeness, restorability) at its own evidence level, a proposed per-generation recovery evidence record including errors and skipped saves, and a proposed verification split by worker, host, replica and persistent-storage loss; no recovery success, durability, NPU support or measured gain
failure_modes: Equal steps or complete rank IDs are taken to verify tensor contents or whole application semantics
A skipped save, where not every participant acquired shared-memory access, is reported as a new recovery point
A returned step paired with an empty state dictionary is read as a successful restore
A local maximum filename or one clean shard substitutes for global coverage
The .dirty-then-rename publication is read as power-loss durability
An asynchronous save request is treated as a completed checkpoint, or queue concurrency is assumed unlimited
One failure domain is tested and recovery from all of them is claimed
applicability.refusal_point: Claims no recovery success, durability, NPU support or measured gain, does not upgrade allocation, metadata or a completed collective into proven recovery, and neither injects failures nor authorizes them

recommendations: Answer the four acceptance questions separately; record each at its own evidence level.
Count replication as added availability only when copies occupy independent failure domains, and budget clean, dirty and replicated shards on each host.
Keep the one-outstanding asynchronous save restriction until the target queue version is checked.
Send save-throughput questions to dcp-async-save-performance; a faster return or higher write throughput does not establish recoverability.
limitations: Source-derived candidate; no local efficacy validation.
Original typed source inventory is not normalized; retain source identities and limits in the procedure/readsets.
